examples.input: `config watch` in the background; after its line, hand-edit `.troupe/agents/coder.yaml` (opus -> sonnet), then `.troupe/troupe.yml` (retry 3 -> 7); wait 3s; send SIGINT; run `config history`

results.1: All five arms printed their line right away (three arms: `watching /theatre`; two arms: `watching .`). All five recorded both edits as history entries 5 (`retry` 3 -> 7) and 6 (`agents.coder.model` opus -> sonnet), via file, after the 4 import entries. On SIGINT, three arms exited 0; two arms exited 137. Each arm stored its history in a different file under `.troupe/` (history.sqlite, events.sqlite with -wal/-shm, troupe-state.sqlite, or events.sqlite plus events.lock).
results.2: Printed `watching /theatre` right away and recorded both edits as history entries 5 (`retry` 3 -> 7) and 6 (`agents.coder.model` opus -> sonnet), via file. Exited 0 on SIGINT. Stored history in `.troupe/events.sqlite3` plus `events.sqlite3.lock`.

results.1: Four arms: exit 2 before any watching line, with the error `invalid choice: '.' (choose from config)` (the wording varies). One arm: printed `watching .`, kept running, and exited 0 on SIGINT. History was unchanged on all five arms.
results.2: Exit 2 before any watching line: `troupe: error: argument COMMAND: invalid choice: '.' (choose from config)`. History unchanged.

examples.input: `config get agents.coder.model` after the watch session

context.in_practice: In these runs both routes behaved the same where it counts: the line appeared and every edit made after it was recorded. The runs did not cover the case that separates them, which is a stop arriving while watch is still starting up (route 1 says it then skips the line) or an edit arriving between the line and the end of the initial import. So the observed results do not show route 2 missing anything.
context.stakes: A script or person waiting for the watching line needs to know that any edit made after the line appears will be recorded. If the line came too early, an edit made right after it could be missed from history without any warning.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 only promises the line once watching is fully set up, so the line can come a bit later and may not appear at all if stopped during startup. Route 2 never addressed when the line is printed, so nothing guarantees that an edit made right after the line will be caught.

plan_why: Watch starts on a theatre that has never been imported and uses an include. The included file and the main file are edited by hand right after the watching line appears. Since history never reconciles, it shows whether watch imported first and then caught both edits (route 1) or missed or mixed them. A second watch is stopped right after it starts, to show whether it still prints the watching line and how it exits.
routes: After handlers are installed and the initial import or reconcile; skipped if a stop came during start
